# SpecStory CLI

`SpecStory` records terminal coding-agent sessions and can wrap supported agents with `specstory run`.

## Installation in This Dotfiles Repo

`specstory` is installed automatically by the `coding_agents` ansible role.

- macOS: Homebrew preferred, with a GitHub release fallback to `~/.local/bin`
- Linux: GitHub release tarball installed to `~/.local/bin`

## Global vs Project Config

This dotfiles repo manages the user-level SpecStory config at `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml`.

SpecStory reads configuration in this order:

1. User-level config: `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml`
2. Project-level config: `./.specstory/cli/config.toml`
3. CLI flags passed to `specstory`

Later sources override earlier ones. That means the dotfile provides global defaults, while a repo-specific `.specstory/cli/config.toml` can override them when a project needs different behavior.

## Managed Defaults

The managed config keeps the upstream sample sections as commented documentation, but only enables `[providers]` defaults.

Configured providers:

- `claude_cmd = "claude --dangerously-skip-permissions"`
- `codex_cmd = 'codex -c model_reasoning_effort="high" --ask-for-approval never --sandbox danger-full-access -c model_reasoning_summary="detailed" -c model_supports_reasoning_summaries=true'`
- `cursor_cmd = "cursor-agent --yolo"`
- `droid_cmd = "droid --yolo"`
- `gemini_cmd = "gemini --sandbox=none"`

These are the commands `specstory run claude`, `specstory run codex`, and similar provider shortcuts will execute by default unless overridden per project or on the command line.

## Safety Tradeoff

The configured provider commands intentionally favor low-friction agent execution:

- Claude uses `--dangerously-skip-permissions`
- Codex uses `--ask-for-approval never` and `--sandbox danger-full-access`
- Cursor and Droid use `--yolo`
- Gemini uses `--sandbox=none`

This removes most interactive permission prompts, which is useful for fast local workflows, but it also gives the wrapped agents broader filesystem or command access. Keep these defaults only if you trust the environment and want convenience over stricter guardrails. If not, override the relevant provider command in the global file, a project-local config, or the `specstory run -c ...` flag.

## Verify

```bash
specstory --version
specstory run codex --help
chezmoi diff
```

## References

- [SpecStory CLI usage docs](https://docs.specstory.com/integrations/terminal-coding-agents/usage#configuration)
- [SpecStory CLI releases](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/releases)

_**Agent (gpt-5.4 2026-04-14 12:23:33Z)**_

There are three separate warnings, with different root causes.

The first one is not a Codex problem at all. It’s SpecStory telling you its own CLI is outdated: your run shows `Current version: 1.6.0` and `Latest version: 1.12.0`. That check is enabled by default in the managed SpecStory config at [private_cli/config.toml](/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/private_dot_specstory/private_cli/config.toml) and documented in [specstory.md](/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/specstory.md).

The sandbox warning is a host/kernel capability problem on Linux. Codex’s sandbox uses `bubblewrap`, which needs unprivileged user namespaces and loopback setup. In this environment, `bwrap` fails with `Failed RTM_NEWADDR: Operation not permitted`, which is the same class of failure Codex warned about. That points to user namespaces or related namespace networking being blocked by the host/container policy, not a repo config issue.

The `codex_apps` warning is a separate MCP startup problem. Codex’s own log says the MCP server failed because it “timed out handshaking with MCP server after 30s” in [codex-tui.log](/home/daviddwlee84/.codex/log/codex-tui.log). Your actual Codex config at [config.toml](/home/daviddwlee84/.codex/config.toml) does not define `[mcp_servers.codex_apps]`, so this is not caused by a bad local server stanza in this repo. The practical root cause is that the built-in `codex_apps` MCP service did not come up within the default 30-second timeout; increasing `startup_timeout_sec` may hide it, but the underlying issue is a slow or unhealthy MCP startup.

One extra detail: `specstory run codex` is wrapping Codex with a custom command from [private_cli/config.toml](/home/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/private_dot_specstory/private_cli/config.toml), including `--ask-for-approval never` and `--sandbox danger-full-access`. That wrapper is relevant to how Codex is launched, but it does not appear to be the root cause of the two warnings above.

        dest: /tmp/glow.tar.gz

        path: /tmp/glow

        dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/glow"
        mode: '0755'

 - name: Install DuckDB CLI via official installer (Debian/Ubuntu, user-level)
   when:
     - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
     - duckdb_check.rc != 0
   block:
     - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists (duckdb)
       ansible.builtin.file:
         path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
         state: directory
         mode: '0755'
 
-    - name: Install DuckDB CLI
-      ansible.builtin.shell: |
-        curl -fsSL https://install.duckdb.org | sh
-      args:
-        executable: /bin/bash
+    - name: Set DuckDB release architecture
+      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
+        duckdb_release_arch: >-
+          {{
+            'amd64' if ansible_facts['architecture'] in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
+            else 'arm64' if ansible_facts['architecture'] in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
+            else ''
+          }}
+
+    - name: Fail on unsupported architecture for DuckDB official downloads
+      when: duckdb_release_arch == ''
+      ansible.builtin.fail:
+        msg: "Unsupported architecture for DuckDB official downloads: {{ ansible_facts['architecture'] }}"
+
+    - name: Get DuckDB install page
+      ansible.builtin.uri:
+        url: https://duckdb.org/install/
+        return_content: true
+      register: duckdb_install_page
+
+    - name: Set DuckDB version facts
+      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
+        duckdb_version: "{{ duckdb_install_page.content | regex_search('Installation\\s+Version\\s+([0-9.]+)\\s+\\(current\\)', '\\1') | first }}"
+
+    - name: Fail if DuckDB version could not be parsed
+      when: duckdb_version | default('') == ''
+      ansible.builtin.fail:
+        msg: "Could not determine current DuckDB version from https://duckdb.org/install/"
+
+    - name: Download DuckDB CLI zip
+      ansible.builtin.get_url:
+        url: "https://install.duckdb.org/v{{ duckdb_version }}/duckdb_cli-linux-{{ duckdb_release_arch }}.zip"
+        dest: /tmp/duckdb_cli.zip
+        mode: '0644'
+
+    - name: Create DuckDB temp directory
+      ansible.builtin.file:
+        path: /tmp/duckdb
+        state: directory
+        mode: '0755'
+
+    - name: Extract DuckDB CLI zip
+      ansible.builtin.unarchive:
+        src: /tmp/duckdb_cli.zip
+        dest: /tmp/duckdb
+        remote_src: true
+
+    - name: Find DuckDB binary
+      ansible.builtin.find:
+        paths: /tmp/duckdb
+        patterns: duckdb
+        file_type: file
+        recurse: true
+      register: duckdb_find
+
+    - name: Fail if DuckDB binary was not found in extracted archive
+      when: duckdb_find.matched | default(0) | int == 0
+      ansible.builtin.fail:
+        msg: "DuckDB binary was not found under /tmp/duckdb after extraction"
+
+    - name: Install DuckDB CLI
+      ansible.builtin.copy:
+        src: "{{ duckdb_find.files[0].path }}"
+        dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/duckdb"
+        mode: '0755'
+        remote_src: true
+
+    - name: Clean up DuckDB temp files
+      ansible.builtin.file:
+        path: "{{ item }}"
+        state: absent
+      loop:
+        - /tmp/duckdb_cli.zip
+        - /tmp/duckdb
 
 - name: Verify DuckDB CLI is available
   when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
   ansible.builtin.command: duckdb --version

# --- sesh (tmux session manager) ---
- name: Check if sesh is installed
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  ansible.builtin.command: sesh --version
  register: sesh_check
  changed_when: false
  failed_when: false

- name: Install sesh from GitHub releases (Debian/Ubuntu, user-level)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - sesh_check.rc != 0
  block:
    - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists (sesh)
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    - name: Get latest sesh release
      ansible.builtin.uri:
        url: https://api.github.com/repos/joshmedeski/sesh/releases/latest
        return_content: true
      register: sesh_release

    - name: Set sesh architecture mapping
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        sesh_arch: >-
          {{
            'amd64' if ansible_facts['architecture'] in ['x86_64', 'amd64']
            else 'arm64' if ansible_facts['architecture'] in ['aarch64', 'arm64']
            else ansible_facts['architecture']
          }}

    - name: Download sesh tarball
      ansible.builtin.get_url:
        url: "https://github.com/joshmedeski/sesh/releases/download/{{ sesh_release.json.tag_name }}/sesh_Linux_{{ sesh_arch }}.tar.gz"
        dest: /tmp/sesh.tar.gz
        mode: '0644'

    - name: Extract sesh
      ansible.builtin.unarchive:
        src: /tmp/sesh.tar.gz
        dest: /tmp
        remote_src: true

    - name: Install sesh to ~/.local/bin
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        src: /tmp/sesh
        dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/sesh"
        mode: '0755'
        remote_src: true

    - name: Clean up sesh temp files
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ item }}"
        state: absent
      loop:
        - /tmp/sesh.tar.gz

This was another repo-side bug.

Root cause: the `sesh` task assumed the Linux x86_64 asset was named `sesh_Linux_amd64.tar.gz`, but the current upstream release `v2.25.0` publishes `sesh_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz` instead. - maps `amd64` to `x86_64`
- selects the actual asset from the GitHub release JSON
- creates `/tmp/sesh`, extracts there, finds the binary recursively, and installs it
- fails with a direct message if the asset or binary is missing

`ansible-playbook --syntax-check dot_ansible/playbooks/linux.yml` passes after the change.

`specify-cli` is the CLI from GitHub Spec Kit for spec-driven development workflows.

## Installation in This Dotfiles Repo

`specify-cli` is installed automatically by the `coding_agents` ansible role using `uv`.

Install command used by the role:

uv tool install specify-cli --from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git

specify check
